en.title: Minimum Operations to Make a Binary Palindrome
en.description:
Given a non-negative integer N. One operation adds 1 to or subtracts 1 from the current integer (the result cannot be less than 0). A number is a binary palindrome if its standard binary representation reads the same from left to right as from right to left. Find the minimum number of operations needed to turn N into any binary palindrome.

This site's input range: 0≤N≤2000000000. The OAMaster snapshot gives no additional constraints; this range is included according to the constraints listed in the snapshot.

Original source: https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/google#56-minimum-operations-to-make-binary-palindromic (fixed snapshot content fingerprint b44446404ff98e6bf74fd5f10b0b0a052137ca8517023ae77b14aa159093ea8d).
en.output: Output the minimum number of operations.
en.explanation: Enumerate binary palindromes of at most 31 bits and take the minimum absolute difference from N. For each bit length, only the first-half candidates, which determine the palindrome by symmetry, need to be constructed; the candidates closest to N come from N's corresponding prefix and its adjacent prefixes, and the smallest and largest palindromes of that bit length are checked as well.
hints: Enumerate the number of binary digits of the target palindrome.
Once the number of digits is fixed, the second half of a palindrome is uniquely determined by its first half.
